Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement/legal side (copied Tom):

- Preference: AWS Marketplace Private Offer would be our first choice if Redwood supports a Private Offer route with the same SKU/pricing. That path makes it straightforward for our FinOps to manage spend and for us to issue a PO via AWS.
- If Marketplace is not possible for certain discounts or committed terms, procurement will fall back to issuing a PO to Redwood directly.
- Standard terms: GreenLeaf typically requests net 30 on POs and a 30-day review window for any vendor MSA redlines.
- Timeline: once we have the vendor onboarding form and the draft MSA, legal will take ~2 weeks and procurement ~1–2 weeks after legal signs off. So plan for ~3–4 weeks to issue a PO if everything is standard.

Requested items for your side:
1) Pricing sheet and offered SKU(s) for AWS Marketplace (if available).
2) Draft MSA and any sample Private Offer language.
3) Vendor onboarding form (we attached ours to this reply).
4) High-level estimate for monthly spend to scope approvals (ballpark is fine).

I attached GreenLeaf_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (stub). If you can get those items across today/tomorrow, I’ll route to legal and procurement for an initial review.

Best,

Alicia / Tom — great, thanks for the clarity and the form. Quick answers and options so procurement can pick the path that fits best: 

Commercial paths we support (summary):
1) AWS Marketplace Private Offer (recommended if you want PO routing through AWS):
   - We can create a Private Offer with the SKU(s) that match the committed monthly quantity/discount.
   - Pros: purchase appears on your AWS invoice, FinOps-friendly, AWS handles invoicing to you; still supports committed discounts & term commitments.
   - Cons: private offers sometimes need a brief AWS sales / marketplace setup step; timing depends on AWS approvals (usually < 2 weeks once offer details are set).

2) Direct PO to Redwood (standard vendor invoicing):
   - We issue invoices to GreenLeaf on net 30 after PO.
   - Pros: no AWS intermediation; Redwood legal handles the MSA directly.
   - Cons: procurement routing might take longer if they prefer marketplace consolidation.

Attachments included: Pricing_Sheet_Redwood_Marketplace.csv (SKU-level pricing, stub) and Draft_MSA_Redwood_v1.docx (stub).

Requested from you:
- Please confirm preferred path (Marketplace private offer vs Direct PO).
- If Marketplace, confirm the AWS account ID to which we should create the Private Offer and any internal PO workflow details.
- If Direct PO, share the billing contact and PO issuance cadence.

Proposed next step: 30-min procurement handoff with our finance lead + legal (we suggested Tue 12/07 10:00 AM PT — does that work?).

Thanks — we’ll standby and prioritize based on the path you pick.

Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
